question: Does the pod's token budget, and not its compute, explain why its cards are unquotable?
why_it_matters: Every open-ended card the RunPod 3090 has produced reads done_reason 'length' and parses to nothing, so n is 0 and no card can reach the n>=30 floor in scripts/sign_mill_cards.py. If the cause is the budget, the 3090 is not failing to measure; it is being asked to answer in fewer tokens than the model needs.

setup.prompt: the worker's own: item text + 'Reply with exactly one label and no other text: [labels]'

finding: At the budget the jobs actually use, 64, not one of the 36 answers completed: all 36 ended 'length' and 0 parsed. At 512, 33 of 36 completed and parsed. The model is a reasoning model, so the budget is spent before the label is emitted. This is an instrument setting, not a capability of the model and not a limit of the hardware.
what_this_does_NOT_establish: It does not say the model is accurate. Nothing here was graded against the expected labels; parseable only means one label was emitted. It also does not make prior pod cards valid: they remain unquotable.
consequence_if_changed: max_tokens is part of the instrument. Raising it changes the instrument hash, so results after the change are a NEW series and are not comparable with anything measured at 64. That is a ruling for the measurement lane, not a config tweak, which is why this file states the evidence and stops.
reproduce: the script is /tmp/tokbudget.py on the pod; 72 generations, no key, no network beyond loopback Ollama
